source_title: Xena: Warrior Princess — Season 1 Episode 1 opening witness
continuity_scope: Xena: Warrior Princess television continuity only, restricted to Season 1 Episode 1, “Sins of the Past,” as identified and synopsized by NBCUniversal’s SYFY, plus the episode’s primary on-screen ending for the Xena–Gabrielle travel decision. Universal’s rights-holder complete-series page is used only to identify Gabrielle as the series companion, never for later events. Hercules: The Legendary Journeys episodes, comics, novels, games, and later Xena episodes/seasons are excluded except that the spin-off relationship is noted only as excluded context.
work_or_witnesses: Xena: Warrior Princess, Season 1 Episode 1: “Sins of the Past”
NBCUniversal SYFY official episode page and synopsis
Universal Pictures At Home rights-holder series page
coverage_rule: Include the named individual dramatic characters directly established by the official episode synopsis or required to represent its primary ending: Xena, Draco, and Gabrielle. Other named/credited episode figures are omitted because the declared official synopsis does not make them central claim-bearing figures in this pass, and no non-official credit database is used to expand the cohort. Warrior/bard roles, warlords, gods/mythic beings, magic, artifacts, places, tribes, slavery, and historical/mythological-adaptation context are terms or omissions, not character nodes unless directly supported by this witness.
omissions: All individual figures not included by the declared official-synopsis/primary-ending coverage rule, including named or unnamed episode villagers, family members, soldiers, and mythic beings.

All Hercules: The Legendary Journeys episodes and crossover plot, except the fact that it is a separate excluded television context; all later Xena episodes/seasons; comics, novels, games, and other adaptations.
Gods, mythic beings, magic systems, artifacts, tribes, place histories, bard identity, and Greek-mythological identities not directly supplied by the selected episode synopsis/ending.

Sexuality, queerness, romance, marriage, consent, slavery/exploitation details, gender identity, ethnicity/cultural coding, disability, trauma, exact violence/death events, and historical or mythological equivalence claims that are absent from the declared evidence.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, recaps, social posts, unlicensed transcripts, and retrospective relationship labels.
uncertainties: SYFY says Xena atones for an evil past by defending her home village from Draco. It does not enumerate the past acts, establish their legal/moral classification beyond that wording, or make forgiveness/reconciliation a completed outcome.

The episode’s primary ending supplies that Gabrielle joins Xena’s travel. It does not establish a sexual/romantic relationship, a permanent partnership, a power imbalance conclusion, or any later label; the Universal series-page phrase ‘faithful friend’ is not used as episode-one relationship proof.
The official synopsis calls Draco a marauding warlord but does not supply ethnicity, peoplehood, historical period, a Greek-myth identity, political legitimacy, or a complete military organization.

This historical-fantasy television program may borrow classical imagery, but no episode-one claim is treated as evidence about ancient Greece, an actual historical society, or a faithful adaptation of a particular myth.
SYFY’s synopsis contains a defense against a marauding warlord. No specific injuries, deaths, captivity, slavery, disability, or trauma diagnosis is stated or inferred in this pass.
evidence_basis: NBCUniversal SYFY’s official Episode 1 page supplies the episode identity, broadcast date, Xena, Draco, evil-past/atonement, and home-village-defense claims. The primary episode ending is the only evidence used for Gabrielle’s joining of Xena; Universal Pictures At Home corroborates Gabrielle’s rights-holder series identity but is not used to import later continuity.
